examples: He clomped heavily up the stairs in his boots.
The great clod trod heavily on my toes!

quotes.text: The departure was not unduly prolonged.[…]Within the door Mrs. Spoker hastily imparted to Mrs. Love a few final sentiments on the subject of Divine Intention in the disposition of buckets;[…]; a deep, guttural instigation to the horse; and the wheels of the waggonette crunched heavily away into obscurity.

senses.definition: To a considerable degree, to a great extent.
examples: He relied heavily on the data collected by the others.
Your advice still weighs heavily with me.
This problem weighs heavily on my mind.

quotes.text: An indulgent playmate, Grannie would lay aside the long scratchy-looking letter she was writing (heavily crossed ‘to save notepaper’) and enter into the delightful pastime of ‘a chicken from Mr Whiteley's’.

quotes.text: In Virginia, gone are the weekly outings to Walmart to stock up on provisions; to El Ranchito, the Mexican convenience store, to buy shell-shaped concha pastries; and to the laundromat to machine wash heavily soiled garments.

senses.definition: In a manner designed for heavy duty.
examples: heavily armed soldiers; heavily armoured tanks; heavily reinforced walls

quotes.text: Nanny Broome was looking up at the outer wall. Just under the ceiling there were three lunette windows, heavily barred and blacked out in the normal way by centuries of grime.

senses.definition: So as to be thick or heavy.
examples: heavily built young men; his heavily muscled arms
